qobuz_limit.description: The daily limit setting of Qobuz (kept for one release).

qobuz_needed.description: The downloads the plan needs from Qobuz (kept for one release).

qobuz_uses.description: The downloads expected from Qobuz today (kept for one release).

account_today.description: The first set-up card of `limits()` (Qobuz first, then YouTube Premium, then SoundCloud Go+); null when no service is set up.

DiscardPreviewItem.description: One song of a Discard preview.

file.description: The current file (it stays), an absolute path.

parked.description: The parked better version that is deleted for good, an absolute path.

Doctor.description: `doctor`: everything that is wrong, each problem with what to do next, and every check that ran.

checks.description: Every check, in order, with its state.

problems.description: What was found: problems first, then notes, each in check order.

text.description: The answer in one sentence: how many problems and notes, or that nothing is wrong.

label.description: What the check looks at, in words.

state.description: `ok`: nothing found. `problem` / `note`: it found something of that level (a problem wins). `skipped`: it was not run: it needs a music folder and none is chosen, or it reads the library's records and those cannot be read (the `records` check says so).

DoctorProblem.description: One thing `doctor` found, with what to do about it.

count.description: The number the text counts (jobs, folders, files, tracks); null when it counts nothing.

gig.description: Whether the next gig depends on it (`status --ready` lists these).

level.description: `problem`: something to fix. `note`: worth knowing, nothing to fix.

next.description: Commands that look further or move on.

person_steps.description: The steps only a person can do.

DownloadTool.description: One download tool in Settings → This Mac.

previous.description: What Go back would use; null: nothing to go back to.

source.description: `built_in` came with Discjockey, `updated` was brought by Update download tools.

version.description: What this window runs; null: not installed.

waiting.description: The version the next start uses, when it differs: an update or a step back waits for a reopen.

DownloadTools.description: The two download tools by name: `yt-dlp`, and `streamrip` (always `built_in` with null `waiting` and `previous`). Keyed by name because `yt-dlp` is no identifier.

DownloadsAccount.description: A YouTube or SoundCloud rung of the ladder and its account panel.

browser.description: The browser the login is read from, null when not set up.

browser_name.description: The browser's name, null when not set up.

last_check.description: The last login check; null when never checked since it was saved.

profile.description: The browser profile's folder; null: the default one.

profile_name.description: The profile's display name; null when it can't be read.

state.description: `on`; `off` (not set up, or its last check found no login / failed); `no_premium` (YouTube: a free login, used only for Liked music); `unreadable` (macOS did not let Discjockey read the browser's login); `paused`; `used_up`.

tracks.description: The library's live lossy tracks this account brought in at about 256 kbps.

DownloadsView.description: The source ladder and the account panels of Settings and Setup (spec settings-setup §6.4): each download source's state and the library counted by rung. Without a music folder the library counts are zero.

DownloadsViewLibrary.description: The library's live tracks (in a playlist, not hidden) counted by rung.

account.description: Lossy stream downloads at 200 kbps or more.

lossless.description: Lossless tracks (an artist's lossless original counts here).

DownloadsViewQobuz.description: The Qobuz rung of the ladder.

last_check.description: The last login check; null when never checked since it was saved.

state.description: `on`; `off` (not signed in, or its last login check failed); `skipped` ("I don't have Qobuz"); `paused` (stopped itself today); `used_up` (today's allowance used).

added.description: The playlist day (an ISO time); for an own file the day Discjockey first saw it.

aiff.description: `cdj` items: why Convert can't run now (an `EligibleReason` key), null when it can.

can_undo.description: `rekordbox_check` items: the check belongs to a swap or an added file `undo_upgrade` can still put back.

cdj.description: `cdj` items: what the CDJs refuse in the file.

cover_url.description: The media URL of the embedded cover, else the Spotify image URL, else null (show a placeholder).

cutoff_hz.description: The measured cutoff in Hz, if measured; `quality_label` is its words.

detail.description: The row's short line (what to do, or why it is here).

file_state.description: Whether the item's file is there now (`FileState`), or `no_file`: the song has none (Not found).

folder.description: The playlist folder the file is in; empty for the user's own songs from the import, which belong to no playlist folder.

free.description: The artist gives it away: a not found, weak, good lossy or fake track with a free download (the row's FREE tag). Not sent by the engine on a `rekordbox_check` item (finding).

group.description: The group the item is in.

hidden.description: Whether the user hid the song.

in_playlists.description: Whether a playlist still holds the song.

missing.description: `missing_file` items (issue 43): the song's waiting file, with its action and the engine's words.

own.description: A file of the user's own that the import found (no playlist holds it). Not sent by the engine on a duplicate group's item (finding); a `TrackRow` has it always.

path.description: The file's path (absolute for the user's own songs), or null when there is none.

quality.description: The colour class: lossless green, good_lossy yellow, weak red, fake purple, missing red.

quality_label.description: The words next to the colour: LOSSLESS, 20.0 kHz, LOSSY, FAKE · 16.0 kHz, NOT FOUND.

rev.description: The record's revision (10 hex): send it back as `expect` / `--if-rev` so the write refuses if the song changed since this read.

same_track.description: `upgrade_ready` items: why Same track can't run now (an `EligibleReason` key), null when it can.

source.description: Where the file came from, or null.

source_name.description: The source in short words: Qobuz, YT Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, bought; `own file` for a file the import found.

status.description: What the sound check made of the file.

upgrade_ready.description: Whether a better version is waiting.

DuplicatePair.description: A group of files that are the same audio or the same song: two or more, by file id.

recommended.description: The `file_id` the panel picks to keep (the better sound, then AIFF), null when there is no clear winner.

recommended_why.description: The recommendation's one line ("Recommended: best quality").

why.description: Why the files are one group.

DuplicateWhy.description: Why the files of a group are one group.

Empty.description: An answer or a job result with nothing in it (`{}`).

EmptyKind.description: Why a page has nothing to show (a first-run or empty state), or null when it has something.

ErrorKind.description: What kind of error a report line holds (errors: network, qobuz or other; a song nobody has: not_found).

Estimate.description: The estimate of the dashboard's ready plan.

accounts.description: The expected split between the services.

duration_min.description: How long the downloads that fit today take, in minutes (70 s a download, rounded to 5 minutes).

left.description: Today's remaining allowance; null: no daily limit (only free sources are set up).

qobuz_left.description: What is left of Qobuz's allowance today (kept for one release).

qobuz_limit.description: The daily limit setting of Qobuz (kept for one release).

qobuz_needed.description: The downloads the plan needs from Qobuz (kept for one release).

qobuz_uses.description: The downloads expected from Qobuz today (kept for one release).

EstimateAccount.description: Which service the downloads are expected to use: one entry per set-up service, in quality order.

about.description: True for every service but Qobuz: an estimate.

left.description: What is left of its allowance today.

uses.description: How many downloads it is expected to do; null for an account behind Qobuz, which only gets the tracks Qobuz lacks.

EstimateBase.description: The plan's estimate without its accounts. `duration_min` counts only the downloads that fit today (the rest wait for the next sync at once).

duration_min.description: How long the downloads that fit today take, in minutes (70 s a download, rounded to 5 minutes).

left.description: Today's remaining allowance; null: no daily limit (only free sources are set up).

qobuz_left.description: What is left of Qobuz's allowance today (kept for one release).

qobuz_limit.description: The daily limit setting of Qobuz (kept for one release).

qobuz_needed.description: The downloads the plan needs from Qobuz (kept for one release).

qobuz_uses.description: The downloads expected from Qobuz today (kept for one release).

ExtraDay.description: A one-time extra for one day (settings.json `extra_today`).

amount.description: How many extra downloads that day.

FactsPreview.description: The dry run of `library facts`: nothing is stored.

total.description: How many own files lack stored facts.

FactsResult.description: The result of `fill_facts` (`library facts`): the audio facts read for the files that had none (codec, rate, bit depth, bitrate). A second run finds none.

filled.description: The files whose facts were read.

unreadable.description: The files ffprobe found no sound in: marked and left out until they change.

Fail.description: A problem answer: `{ok: false, kind, message}` and, from the bridge decorator, the command line's view of it (issue 39, `discjockey/hub/outcomes.py`); the window ignores the latter. `outcome`, `reason`, `next`, `person_steps` and `data` are always present on an answer of the engine, optional here so the fake bridge needs no change. The window never sends what makes a `bad_args`: a failure the command line gets is a `CliFail`.

data.description: Facts that belong to the reason, a different object per reason (`outcomes.REASONS`); null or absent when there are none.

kind.description: Why it failed; the window reads this.

outcome.description: The command line's outcome of the problem.

person_steps.description: The steps only a person can do.

reason.description: The closed reason of the problem (`outcomes.REASONS`).

service.description: Set when a playlist service caused the problem (a SourceError); absent for every other.

setting.description: Only with kind `setting_off` (add_playlist for a link that needs a Settings choice that is off).

FailKind.description: The `kind` of a failed answer: a `ProblemKind`, or `bad_args` for what only the command line sends (a typed id or word that names nothing; the window never sends one and shows it as `crashed`).

FailNext.description: One command that moves on after a problem.

FailOutcome.description: The command line's outcome of a problem (`outcomes.KIND_OUTCOME`).

FailPersonStep.description: One step only a person can do.

say.description: What the person does, in words.

then.description: The command that goes on afterwards, or null.

Favourite.description: A Favourite, resolved. Keys whose playlist or folder is gone are left out of the answer (the engine keeps them stored, also through a `set_favourites` that does not name them).

count.description: A playlist's songs (null: never read) or a folder's files.

enabled.description: A playlist's switch; true for a folder.

kind.description: A playlist or a folder.

name.description: The playlist's folder name, or a crate's `label`.

path.description: The folder's path; null for a playlist.

service.description: A playlist's service; null for a folder.

state.description: A playlist is `here`; a crate has its watched folder's.

FavouritesSaved.description: What `set_favourites` answers: a brief save that starts no job.

favourites.description: The keys now stored, in order.

FileSide.description: One file of a question or of a duplicate group. `path` is absolute for an import folder's file.

audio_url.description: The media URL to play; null only for a file that is offline or can't be played (an import folder's file plays through `file/<file_id>`).

in_playlist.description: Whether the file is the library's file of a playlist song.

online.description: The file is there by the folder rule only (`here`), not offline.

path.description: The file's path.

quality_label.description: The words next to the colour.

song_key.description: The song the file is linked to, or null.

FileState.description: Whether a file is there now: `here`; `offline` (its drive is not connected); `folder_missing` (its watched folder is not found); `file_missing` (the folder is there, the file's path is not: it went since the last scan, or its row waits as missing).

FindLogins.description: `find_logins(service)`: the installed browsers, the default first, and which profiles hold a login.

browsers.description: The installed browsers, the default one first.

FindTracksAnswer.description: The songs that match, in artist then title order. With no hit and playlists read long ago, `next` says to read them.

next.description: `sync read`, when there is no hit and the playlists were read before their last change or more than a day ago.

kind.description: What a usable folder holds; null when it is not usable.

message.description: The refusal in plain words; null when usable.

path.description: The resolved folder.

problem.description: Why it is not usable, else null.

usable.description: Whether it can be the music folder; false: `problem` names why.

FolderKind.description: What a usable folder holds: `new` (not there yet, made on the user's choice), `empty`, `discjockey_library` (a Discjockey library already) or `other_files` (the page asks before using it).

FolderProblem.description: Why a folder can't be the music folder.

FolderState.description: Where a folder is now: `here`, `offline` (its drive is not connected) or `folder_missing` (not found: moved, renamed, deleted); the innermost watched folder that is away decides, for its crates too.

path.description: The file's absolute path; null without a file.

rel_path.description: The file's path relative to the music folder; null without a file and for a file of an import folder.

FreeDownload.description: The artist's free download of a SoundCloud version: a gate page (follow, like or e-mail) or SoundCloud's own download button.

direct.description: SoundCloud's own download button, not a gate page.

url.description: The page to open (SoundCloud's own page when `direct`).

Freshness.description: How fresh the answers are, from the stored records alone: never a scan or a fetch.

read_at.description: When the playlists were last read, an ISO time; null when none was.

scanned_at.description: When the index was last scanned (a watched folder's last scan), an ISO time; null while there is no music folder, no library.db or nothing was scanned.

History.description: What changed and what can be undone: runs, batches and single steps, newest first.

since.description: The time the list starts at, an ISO time; null when it was not limited.

HistoryEntry.description: One thing that changed: a run of the sync, a batch (AIFF or moves) or a single step Discjockey logged. Exactly one of `undo` and `cant_text` is set.

artist.description: The song's artist, for a single step.

at.description: When it happened, an ISO time: a run's or batch's start, a step's time.

cant_text.description: Why `undo` is null, in words; null when there is an `undo`.

id.description: The id the commands take: `report:<stamp>`, `aiff:12` or `moves:12`; null for a single step.

kind.description: A run, a batch or a single logged step.

title.description: The song's title, for a single step.

track_id.description: The song a single step was done to; null for a run or a batch.

undo.description: The command that undoes it (run its `--dry-run` first); null when nothing does or the command is not there yet.

kind.description: `import` for a usable folder, else null.

merge_hints.description: One line each ("{name} is inside it and becomes part of it.").

merges.description: The paths of the watched folders inside it that it would take over (their files and links are kept).

path.description: The resolved folder.

problem.description: Why it can't be watched, else null.

usable.description: Whether it can be watched; false: `problem` names why.

ImportFolderProblem.description: Why a folder can't be watched: a `FolderProblem`, or `not_readable`, `not_found`, `music` (inside the music folder), `holds_music` (holds it), `watched` (inside a watched folder) or `already`.

ImportPhase.description: A phase of the import (`ImportProgress` events).

ImportResult.description: The result of the `import` job (`add_watched_folder`, `start_import`), also of a stopped one (`stopped` true).

files.description: The files imported (read in either pass, not unreadable now).

left.description: The files the next import still works through.

link_note.description: The words of a link that did not happen, else null.

sound_checked.description: The files whose sound was checked.

unreadable.description: The files it could not read.

action.description: What was done: same_track, add_new, convert, rename, ...

path.description: The file's path.

rekordbox.description: What was written in rekordbox, or null.

ItemResultRekordbox.description: What was written in rekordbox for one track.

kept.description: The fields kept as the user edited them.

JobEvents.description: What `job_events` answers: a job's events from a position on (the window's follow of a job another process runs).

done.description: The job has ended and these were its last events.

events.description: The job's events from `after` on, as events.ts `HubEvent` objects (`{type, …fields}`), at most 500.

finished.description: The job's end, from its result.json, as the watch sends it (a `JobFinished` event object; `worker_lost` when it left no result); null until `done`.

next.description: The position to ask from next: `after` plus the lines of the files delivered (a line that is no event has its place but is not in `events`).

status.description: The job's status when it was read.

JobSnap.description: A job's snapshot after a window reload (the events are not shapes: `tests/fixtures/hub_events.schema.json` pins them).

actions.description: The run's planned actions in the order the run does them; empty until a run started and for jobs without a run.

batch_kind.description: An AIFF batch job's (`upgrade_batch`, `aiff_batch`, `batch_resume`, `upgrade_add_new`, `upgrade_discard`) batch kind, else null: `upgrade` for Same track, `convert` for what Convert, Give it its clean name, Make all and the CDJ group's Convert all start; for `batch_resume` the stopped batch's own kind. After a reload it says whose batch runs; the live `JobStarted` event carries the same.

finished.description: The `JobFinished` event as events.ts `HubEvent`, null while the job runs.

kind.description: The job kind (`sync`, `refresh`, `tidy`, ...).

last.description: The newest event of each type, as events.ts `HubEvent`, by the event's type name.

results.description: The `ActionFinished` events so far, as events.ts `HubEvent`s, in a list.

started.description: When it started, an ISO time.

stopping.description: A stop was asked and the job ends after its current step.

track_id.description: The song the job works on; null for a job on none.

usage.description: The newest `AccountUsage` event of each service, in the order the services first reported (`last` keeps only the newest one overall); empty until a download counted.

JobStatus.description: The snapshot after a window reload.

console.description: Who holds the library lock besides this window, the Terminal's job or another window's; null when nothing does. After a reload the banner names the job from it at once.

job.description: The running write job; null when none runs.

last_sync.description: The newest sync of this music folder, the window's or the terminal's: what was ticked, and when it ended; null with none.

read_status.description: How the last playlists read went.

sign_in.description: A sign-in waiting for the browser (its own slot beside the write jobs; Settings restores its phase from it); null when none.

KeepFileResult.description: The result of `keep_file`, also of a job that stopped after some moves (then `kept_track` is null).

kept_track.description: The key of the song the kept file belongs to afterwards (a playlist song may have taken the file over from an own song); null when the file is linked to no song, or the job stopped before the end.

recovered.description: What a recovery of an earlier crash put right, `[what, ok]` per line.

results.description: One report line per file that went to Superseded/, in the order they moved: `section` `replaced`, `path` where the file went (relative to the music folder). Fewer than the group's other files when a move stopped the job.

LastCheck.description: A saved login check (settings.json): when it ran and what it found.

at.description: When the check ran, an ISO time.

kbps.description: The stream quality found, else null.

LastSync.description: The newest sync of this music folder, from the job registry.

ended.description: When it ended, an ISO time; null while it runs.

Library.description: One view of the library. A playlist or folder that is not there any more is no error: `empty` is `gone`, `rows` and `subtitle` are empty. An empty folder, and a playlist that was read and holds nothing, both have `empty` `no_match` even without search text.

aiff_stopped.description: The newest stopped `library:*` AIFF batch with items left: the header's "Resume · {left} left"; null when none (issue 33 stage D).

also.description: A playlist view: the files in the playlist's own Library folder whose song the playlist does not hold, by artist then title; null elsewhere.

chips.description: The row count of each `LibraryFilter` (`all` counts every row the table lists, a read playlist's songs without a file too, never `also`).

empty.description: Why the page has nothing to show (`gone` adds to the usual words), or null.

enabled.description: A playlist view: whether its line is switched on; null elsewhere.

folder.description: The old `folder` argument: null (All tracks), `__not_in_playlist__`, a playlist's folder name or a folder's key.

folder_kind.description: Folder views: what the folder is (`library`: a Library/ folder); null: none of these (`empty` is `gone`).

key.description: The playlist's folder name as playlists.txt spells it, or the folder's path; null for All tracks and Not in a playlist.

read_at.description: A playlist view: when its read was made; null: never read, and in other views.

rows.description: The rows of the view, searched and filtered.

service.description: A playlist view: its service; null elsewhere.

songs.description: A read playlist's songs: how many it lists and how many have a file; null elsewhere and while never read. The page words "13 of 18 downloaded".

subtitle.description: The header's second line as parts in order of importance (the page drops the last parts first); empty when `gone`.

LibraryAiffStopped.description: The newest stopped `library:*` AIFF batch (Make all, a selection's Convert) with items left.

left.description: How many items are left ("Resume · {left} left").

LibraryFileState.description: A row's file as the Library says it: a `FileState`, or `no_file` for a playlist song that has no file yet (only in a playlist view).

LibraryRow.description: One row of the Library: a song's row with what the table needs. The user's own songs (the import) are in no folder: `folder` is empty and `in_playlists` false.

added.description: The playlist day (an ISO time); for an own file the day Discjockey first saw it.

cover_url.description: The media URL of the embedded cover, else the Spotify image URL, else null (show a placeholder).

cutoff_hz.description: The measured cutoff in Hz, if measured; `quality_label` is its words.

file_state.description: Whether the row's file is there now, decided per watched folder (`file_missing` is the stored mark of a file that waits as missing, issue 43); a row that is not `here` does not play. `no_file`: a playlist song that has no file yet.

folder.description: The playlist folder the file is in; empty for the user's own songs from the import, which belong to no playlist folder.

hidden.description: Whether the user hid the song.

in_missing_files.description: To-do's Missing files group lists the song: true only for a row whose file waits as missing and that the group lists; false for every other row, and for a song whose Download again is asked.

in_playlists.description: Whether a playlist still holds the song.

next_try.description: A `not_found` row: the day the sync looks again (ISO; due on and after it) or `next_sync` (never looked yet); null on every other row.

own.description: A file of the user's own that the import found (no playlist holds it): the table never dims it. False for a downloaded or bought one.

path.description: The file's path (absolute for the user's own songs), or null when there is none.

place.description: The folder the file sits in, in the Folder column's words (a Library file says its playlist line or folder, a watched folder's file the folder and its crate); null: no file, or a playlist view's rows inside the playlist's own Library folder.

playlists.description: The playlists whose read holds the song, in playlists.txt order; empty for a song only a file holds.

position.description: The place in the playlist's read (playlist view only).

quality.description: The colour class: lossless green, good_lossy yellow, weak red, fake purple, missing red.

quality_label.description: The words next to the colour: LOSSLESS, 20.0 kHz, LOSSY, FAKE · 16.0 kHz, NOT FOUND.

rev.description: The record's revision (10 hex): send it back as `expect` / `--if-rev` so the write refuses if the song changed since this read.

sound_checked.description: False for an imported file whose sound is not judged yet (its quality is the codec's guess for now: the page says "sound not checked yet").

source.description: Where the file came from, or null.

source_name.description: The source in short words: Qobuz, YT Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, bought; `own file` for a file the import found.

status.description: What the sound check made of the file.

subfolder.description: Folder views only: a watched folder's rows carry their crate's label ("" for a file directly in it), a crate's the folders below it ("2019" or "A › B"); null elsewhere.

track_link.description: The song's page on its service, for the row menu's "Open in {Service}"; null: no page known.

upgrade_ready.description: Whether a better version is waiting.

wait.description: A song without a file: `waiting` (the sync has yet to get it) or `not_found` (the sync found nothing usable); null for a row with a file.

LibrarySongs.description: A read playlist's songs, before any search or filter.

listed.description: How many distinct songs it lists (what the sidebar's `songs` counts).

with_file.description: How many of them have a file.

LibrarySort.description: The Library's order: a column name, `-` in front for descending. `order` is a playlist's own order (its read record's); the engine's default there, and `artist` elsewhere.

LibrarySummary.description: The folder at a glance, unaffected by the search and the filter. Only the rows with a file count.

by_quality.description: The checked files by quality class.

lossless_share.description: The share of the checked files that are lossless; null when none is checked.

not_lossless.description: The checked files that are not lossless (good lossy + weak + fake).

to_do.description: What the to-do list shows of the view (in a playlist, not hidden).

LibraryView.description: Which view of the Library: All tracks, Not in a playlist, a playlist or a folder.

folder.description: The folder the Liked music line got (`Liked_music`, or `Liked_music_2`, ... when taken).

LimitCard.description: One service's card on Download limits (always all three, in quality order); a service that is not set up has zeros.

name.description: Its name for the page (Qobuz, YouTube Premium, SoundCloud Go+).

paused.description: Paused by the auto-stop: stored as stopped until the next sync starts. An account also counts an `auto_stop` signal of today.

set_up.description: Whether the service is set up.

warnings.description: Warning signs of the last 14 days.

cards.description: Always all three services in quality order.

service.description: The service the page is for.

usage.description: The page of that service; null when it is not set up.

problem.description: Why it can't be read: `no_access` (Safari without Full Disk Access) or `locked`; else null.

profiles.description: Its profiles and which hold a login.

readable.description: Whether its login files can be read.

LoginBrowserProfile.description: One browser profile and whether it holds a login.

id.description: The profile's folder; null is Safari's only profile.

signed_in.description: Whether the profile holds a login of the service.

MatchCounts.description: How many of each kind there are in the narrowed view.

away.description: Rekordbox tracks on a watched drive that is not connected now.

matched.description: Rekordbox tracks whose file is a song's current file.

missing.description: Rekordbox tracks whose file is not there.

not_in_library.description: Rekordbox tracks whose file is in your music folder or a watched folder but is no song's file.

not_in_rekordbox.description: Files of your library that no rekordbox track holds.
